text.sourceText: When Ferdinand Magellan, the first circumnavigator of the globe, sailed into the islands now known as the Philippine archipelago in 1521, it was reported that the people of the islands sang and chanted sixteen types of songs, various short poems, myths, legends, and epics as they went about their daily living. The native Filipinos “were a singing people.” Their myths and legends reflected the people’s animistic beliefs, and the Spanish friars who followed Magellan found their way of perceiving and explaining the world laughable. For example, instead of an all-powerful God creating man in his own image and woman from the rib of man, the creation myth they encountered in the Philippines recounts how the first man and woman emerged simultaneously from the nodes of a bamboo. These two myths reflect the clash of the native animistic, matriarchal, egalitarian society with the patriarchal beliefs of Spanish Catholicism. Much of the indigenous oral literature was eradicated, and the native priestesses, called babaylan, were persecuted. What parts of this rich culture were not annihilated were infused by the friars with Christian content to accelerate acceptance of Christianity and conversion. Thus the passion of Christ was chanted in a Southeast Asian way; to this day, it is observed by Filipinos all over the Philippines and even in the diaspora. When the Americans came at the turn of the twentieth century, Hispanized native culture was firmly established.
text.id: Ketika Ferdinand Magellan, pertama civigator dunia, berlayar ke pulau-pulau sekarang dikenal sebagai archipelago Filipina pada tahun 1521, dilaporkan bahwa orang-orang pulau bernyanyi dan dinyanyikan enam belas jenis lagu, berbagai puisi pendek, mitos, legenda, dan epital saat mereka pergi tentang kehidupan sehari-hari mereka. Orang Filipina asli "adalah orang bernyanyi" mitos dan legenda mereka mencerminkan kepercayaan animistik orang-orang, dan biarawan Spanyol yang mengikuti Magellan menemukan cara mereka untuk memahami dan menjelaskan dunia menggelikan. Sebagai contoh, daripada semua-kuat Allah menciptakan manusia dalam gambar-Nya sendiri dan wanita dari tulang rusuk manusia, mitos penciptaan yang mereka temui di Filipina menceritakan bagaimana orang pertama dan wanita muncul secara bersamaan dari node bambu. Kedua mitos ini mencerminkan bentrokan dari animistik asli, matriarchal, masyarakat egaliterian dengan keyakinan patriarkal dari Katolik Spanyol sebagian besar literatur oral pribumi dihapuskan, dan pendeta-pendeta pribumi, yang disebut babaylan, dianiaya. Bagian mana dari budaya kaya ini yang tidak dimusnahkan yang ditanamkan oleh biarawan dengan konten Kristen untuk mempercepat penerimaan Kristen dan konversi. sehingga gairah Kristus dinyanyikan dengan cara Asia Tenggara; sampai hari ini, itu diamati oleh Filipina di seluruh Filipina dan bahkan di diaspora. Ketika Amerika datang pada pergantian abad ke-20, budaya asli Hispanized adalah tegas didirikan.

text.sourceText: The American occupation of the Philippines from 1898 to 1946 opened the floodgates for the Americanization of Filipino tastes, values, and culture. The Americans brought vaudeville to Philippine stage and other forms of entertainment. The mass media—radio, television, movies, and American magazines—and the American public educational system, which imposed an American curriculum and English as the medium of instruction from grade school to graduate school, facilitated the wholesale acceptance of American culture and ways of thinking. English became the language of power, government, and education and was an effective tool in the dissemination of American culture. Filipinos followed and imitated the new trends in American arts and cinema, particularly those conveyed by Hollywood. Thus, there are a Fred Astaire, Elvis Presley, and Charlie Chaplin of the Philippines as well as Elizabeth Taylor look-alikes and musical extravaganzas on film patterned after Hollywood. But despite strong American influence, indigenous culture and Spanish Catholicism remained alive and can be discerned in such box office–hit films with folkloric content as Ang Panday (The Blacksmith), Pepeng Agimat (Jose the Bearer of Talisman) and Darna, the Philippines’ wonder woman who existed long before Wonder Woman became a hit in the United States.
text.id: Amerika pendudukan Filipina dari tahun 1898 sampai 1946 membuka pintu gerbang untuk Amerikanisasi selera Filipina, nilai, dan budaya orang Amerika membawa vaudeville ke panggung Filipina dan bentuk hiburan lainnya. Media massa - radio, televisi, film, dan majalah Amerika - dan sistem pendidikan publik Amerika, yang dikenakan kurikulum Amerika dan Inggris sebagai medium instruksi dari sekolah dasar ke sekolah pascasarjana, memfasilitasi penerimaan keseluruhan budaya Amerika dan cara berpikir. Bahasa Inggris menjadi bahasa kekuasaan, pemerintah, dan pendidikan dan merupakan alat yang efektif dalam penyebaran budaya Amerik. terutama yang disampaikan oleh Hollywood. Jadi, ada Fred Astaire, Elvis Presley, dan Charlie Chaplin dari Filipina serta Elizabeth Taylor looks-alikes dan musikal extraanzas di film berpola setelah Hollywood. Tapi meskipun pengaruh kuat Amerika, budaya adat dan Katolik Spanyol tetap hidup dan dapat dilihat dalam kotak kantor-hit film dengan konten fokloric sebagai Ang Panday (Blacksmith), Pepeng Agimat (Jose Pembawa Talisman) dan Darna, wanita Filipina 'bertanya-tanya lama sebelum Wonder Woman menjadi hit di Amerika Serikat.

text.sourceText: Contemporary music and film are two important mediums for popular culture in the Philippines. Through them one is introduced to ideas, perspectives, and influences present in the everyday lives of Filipinos. And just as the people of the Philippines encompass a variety of languages, dialects, religions, political views, and customs, the music of the islands draws on many sources. These varied sources are implicit in the term Original Pinoy or Original Philippine Music—OPM—which refers to music created by Filipinas and Filipinos that draws inspiration from the many traditional Philippine songs and employs indigenous instruments from the different regions. Besides local kundiman love songs, the genre is influenced by pop, folk, rock, and ballad songs mainly from the United States and from top Western bands like the Beatles that achieved commercial success during the 1960s and 1970s. Some of the more famous OPM artists in the sixties and seventies include Jose Mari Chan, Pilita Corrales, Nora Aunor, the APO Hiking Society, and Freddie Aguilar. Aguilar in particular received worldwide acclaim for his song “Anak” (“Child”) (1977). His rendition of the plaintive, patriotic song “Bayan Ko” (“My Country”) (1980) from the pen of popular nationalist poet Jose Corazon de Jesus and set to music in the 1920s by Constancio de Guzman, became the anthem for the People Power Revolution of the 1980s. A popular protest song, “Bayan Ko” has been sung during crucial moments in Philippine history, first against the American occupation of the Philippines in the 1920s and later in the struggle for national democracy in the seventies and eighties. It was also sung during the funeral of the first female president, Corazon C. Aquino, in 2009. Rock’n’ roll was introduced in the 1950s, but the 1990s are notable for the emergence of bands like the Eraserheads (1990s), Rivermaya (1993), Yano, (Simple, 1993), Siakol (Free, Happy and Sometimes Naughty State of Mind, 1994), Parokya ni Edgar (Parish of Edgar, 1993), and Radioactive Sago Project (1999). Two of the most successful Filipino-American musicians are Apl. de Ap of the Black-Eyed Peas and Chad Hugo of Neptunes and N.E.R.D. Today, OPM encompasses all music created by and for Filipinos in the Philippines and in foreign lands—even by foreign composers, but intended for performance by Filipinos.
text.id: Musik dan film kontemporer adalah dua media penting untuk budaya populer di Filipina. Dan sama seperti orang-orang Filipina mencakup berbagai bahasa, dialek, agama, pandangan politik, dan adat istiadat, musik pulau-pulau menarik banyak sumber. Sumber-sumber ini implisit dalam istilah Pinoy asli atau Musik Filipina asli - OPM - yang mengacu pada musik yang dibuat oleh Filipinas dan Filipinos yang menarik inspirasi dari banyak lagu Filipina tradisional dan mempekerjakan instrumen pribumi dari daerah yang berbeda. Selain lagu-lagu cinta kundiman lokal, genre dipengaruhi oleh pop, rakyat, rock, dan lagu balada terutama dari Amerika Serikat dan dari atas band Barat seperti Beatles yang mencapai keberhasilan komersial selama 1960-an dan 1970-an. Beberapa seniman OPM yang lebih terkenal di tahun 60-an termasuk Jose Mari Chan, Pilita Corrales, Nora Aunor, Masyarakat Hiking APO, dan Freddie Aguilar. Nya rendition lagu sedih, patriotik "Bayan Ko" ("My Country") (1980) dari pena penyair nasionalis populer Jose Corazon de Jesus dan mengatur untuk musik di tahun 1920-an oleh Constancio de Guzman, menjadi anthem for the People Power Revolution of the 1980. Sebuah lagu protes populer, "Bayan Ko" telah dinyanyikan selama momen-momen penting dalam sejarah Filipina, pertama melawan pendudukan Amerika di Filipina pada tahun 1920 dan kemudian dalam perjuangan untuk demokrasi nasional pada tahun 70-an dan 80-an, juga dinyanyikan selama pemakaman presiden wanita pertama, Corazon C. Aquino, pada tahun 2009. Rock 'n' roll diperkenalkan pada tahun 1950an, tetapi tahun 1990an terkenal untuk munculnya band seperti Eraserheads (1990an), Rivermaya (1993), Yano, (Simple, 1993), Siakol (Free, Happy dan Sometimes Naughty State of Mind, 1994), Parokya Edgar (Paroki Edgar, 1993), dan Radioaktif Proyek (1999). Dua musisi paling sukses Filipino-Amerika adalah Apple. de Ap dari Black- Eyed Peas dan Chad Hugo dari lagu-lagu soundtrack dan N.E.R.D. Hari ini, OPM meliputi semua musik yang dibuat oleh dan untuk Filipinos di Filipina dan di tanah asing - bahkan oleh komposer asing, tetapi dimaksudkan untuk kinerja oleh Filipinos.

text.sourceText: Other genres of music popular in the Philippines are jazz, Bossa Nova, Latino music, R&B, and reggae. Cebu is known as the Reggae Capital of the Philippines. Hip-hop performed by artists from the Philippines and from the United States is recited in dialects such as Tagalog, Illocano, and Cebuano as well as English. Francis Magalona, who is widely regarded as the King of Pinoy Rap, helped bring the genre into the mainstream with his album Yo! This groundbreaking album not only achieved commercial success but was one of the first to articulate complex social messages about drug abuse, political corruption, and poverty in the islands.
text.id: Jenis musik populer di Filipina adalah jazz, Bossa Nova, Latino music, R dan reggae. Cebu dikenal sebagai Reggae Capital Filipina. Francis Magalona, yang dianggap luas sebagai Raja Pinoy Rap, membantu membawa genre ke dalam arus utama dengan album Yo! album inovatif ini tidak hanya mencapai keberhasilan komersial tetapi adalah salah satu yang pertama untuk mengartikulasikan pesan sosial kompleks tentang penyalahgunaan narkoba, korupsi politik, dan kemiskinan di pulau-pulau.

text.sourceText: Eraserheads (1990s) a new breed of pop/alternative rock band
text.id: Eraserheads (1990) generasi baru band rock pop / alternatif

text.sourceText: Philippine cinema is the youngest of all the arts. Film was introduced to the islands in 1897 and, like elsewhere, gradually evolved from silent pictures to talkies and from black-and-white to color. At first, the material was taken from the theater and local literature featuring zarzuelas, a kind of musical theater from Spain. In the 1940s, the war brought reality to the movies, but Japanese censorship restricted content. The 1950s saw the golden age of Philippine cinema, which garnered international recognition with such movies as Genghis Kahn (1950) by Manuel Conde, shown at the Venice and Cannes Film Festival, and Anak Dalita (The Ruins, 1956) by Lamberto Avellana, which won the Golden Harvest Award (Best Picture) at the Asia Pacific Film Festival. The genres that predominated in the 1960s were action, with plenty of Filipino secret agents and cowboys; “bomba,” which literally means “bomb,” a local term for soft pornographic and B movies; comedy; and drama. However, Philippine cinema also has a history of espousing social messages and exploring social and political themes. During the 1970s, film production was tightly regulated by the Board of Censors for Motion Pictures (BCMP), which was formed to ensure that movies would reflect messages approved by the Marcos dictatorship and promote the governing principles of his so-called New Society. Movies that were deemed to portray the government in a bad light were banned. The social and political environment of the 1970s made it challenging to introduce new themes and approaches to the big screen. Yet, film producers emerged who not only pushed against accepted social and political boundaries but also introduced new styles of directing and editing. Some of the most influential film directors of the 1970s and 1980s include Lino Brocka, Ishmael Bernal, Mike de Leon, Peque Gallaga, and Kidlat Tahimik (Silent Lightning) aka Eric de Guia. Brocka’s films often integrated powerful themes pertaining to human rights, national identity, and the LGBTQ (Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer) community. Tahimik would receive the International Critic’s Prize at the Berlin Film Festival for his 1977 experimental film, Mababangong Bangungot (Perfumed Nightmare).
text.id: Film diperkenalkan ke pulau-pulau pada tahun 1897 dan, seperti di tempat lain, secara bertahap berevolusi dari gambar diam ke talkies dan dari hitam-putih ke warna. pada awalnya, materi tersebut diambil dari teater dan literatur lokal menampilkan zarzuelas, semacam teater musik dari Spanyol. Pada tahun 1940-an, perang membawa kenyataan pada film, namun sensor Jepang membatasi konten. Tahun 1950-an menyaksikan era keemasan bioskop Filipina, yang mengumpulkan pengakuan internasional dengan film-film seperti Genghis Kahn (1950) oleh Manuel Conde, yang ditunjukkan di Festival Film Venesia dan Cannes, dan Anak Dalit (Ruins, 1956) oleh Lamberto Avellana, yang memenangkan Penghargaan Harvest Emas (Best Picture) di Festival Film Asia Pasifik. Genre yang didominasi pada tahun 1960 adalah aksi, dengan banyak agen rahasia Filipina dan koboi; "bomba", yang secara harfiah berarti "bom", istilah lokal untuk pornografi lembut dan film B; komedi; dan drama. Selama tahun 1970-an, produksi film diatur ketat oleh Dewan Sensor untuk Motion Pictures (BCMP), yang dibentuk untuk memastikan bahwa film akan mencerminkan pesan-pesan yang disetujui oleh kediktatoran Marcos dan mempromosikan prinsip-prinsip yang disebut New Society. Lingkungan sosial dan politik tahun 1970-an membuatnya menantang untuk memperkenalkan tema baru dan pendekatan ke layar besar. namun, produser film muncul yang tidak hanya mendorong terhadap batasan-batasan sosial dan politik yang diterima tetapi juga memperkenalkan gaya baru mengarahkan dan mengedit. Beberapa sutradara film paling berpengaruh tahun 1970-an termasuk Lino Brocka, Ismael Bernal, Mike de Leon, Peque Gallaga, dan Kidlat Tahimik (Silent Lightning) alias Eric de Guia. Film Brocka seringkali memadukan tema-tema kuat yang berkaitan dengan hak asasi manusia, dan komunitas LGBTQ (Lesbian, Gay, Biseksual, Transgender, dan Queer). Tahimik akan menerima Penghargaan Kritikus Internasional di Festival Film Berlin untuk film eksperimental tahun 1977, Mabangong Bangungot (Perfumed Nightmare).

text.sourceText: Since the 1990s, the Philippine movie and music industries have been unable to compete successfully with their American counterparts due to competitive advantages of Hollywood movies, piracy, overtaxation, and a poor economy. However, with digital technologies widely available and no longer affordable only by corporate entities, a new breed of independent film makers has emerged to share their unique stories and visions, bringing home accolades for the country and offering new hope for the ailing industry. Raymond Red, one of the pioneers of independent and alternative cinemas, brought home the prestigious Palme d’Or at the 2000 Cannes Film Festival for his short film Anino (Shadow). He is one of only two Filipino filmmakers included in the Oxford History of World Cinema. In 2009, Brillante Mendoza bested all other entries to the Cannes Film Festival by bringing home the Best Director award for his film Kinatay (Butchered), about murder and police brutality.
text.id: Sejak tahun 1990-an, Film Filipina dan industri musik telah tidak dapat bersaing dengan sukses dengan rekan-rekan Amerika mereka karena keuntungan kompetitif dari film Hollywood, pembajakan, pajak, dan ekonomi miskin. Namun, dengan teknologi digital yang tersedia secara luas dan tidak lagi terjangkau hanya oleh entitas perusahaan, generasi baru pembuat film independen telah muncul untuk berbagi cerita dan visi unik mereka, membawa pulang akrolasi bagi negara dan menawarkan harapan baru bagi industri yang sakit. Raymond Red, salah satu pelopor film independen dan alternatif, membawa pulang bioskop bergengsi Palme d 'Or di Festival Film Cannes 2000 untuk film pendeknya Anino (Shadow). Pada tahun 2009, Brillante Mendoza mengalahkan semua masukan lainnya ke Festival Film Cannes dengan membawa pulang Penghargaan Direktur Terbaik untuk filmnya Kinatay (Terbantai), tentang pembunuhan dan kebrutalan polisi.

text.sourceText: Alternative film festival in honor of director Lino Brocka, known for relevant and artistic films
text.id: Festival film alternatif untuk menghormati sutradara Lino Brocka, dikenal dengan film relevan dan artistik
